verdicts.title: One audit-ledger write door: six hand-signed inserts become one, guard-pinned
verdicts.ambition_why: A chokepoint plus a comment-stripping guard is the right principal move, but it is a consolidation of code that already works, not a new capability.
verdicts.grounding_why: All 9 write sites, the 7 withAuditSignature copies, the retention update, the alert-door precedent, the registry deviation and the data-model.md heading are exactly where the card says.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Guard is red today on 8 direct writes in 5 files and seeds a prose-only violation; the signing cases pin byte-identical output through the existing per-file tests.
verdicts.notes: No run-1 overlap. Heavy run-2 overlap: scans-persist.ts and org-watch.ts are also in github-data B's write set and scans-persist.ts in roadmap A's; sequence these three in one wave serially. retention.ts (2817 lines) is touched for one update call only. deleteMany at retention.ts:608 is the only ledger delete, as claimed.

verdicts.title: Verify the whole filtered trail in one click, not just the 25 rows on screen
verdicts.ambition_why: Turns the integrity work from a per-page decoration into the question an examiner actually asks, reusing the CSV walk so coverage is identical by construction.
verdicts.grounding_why: AuditTab limit 25, entries-scoped tamperedCount, the CSV cursor loop with CSV_MAX_ROWS 10000 and per-row e.integrity, getAuditLog's verifyAudit per row, and the absence of an integrity/ route all verified.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Route-gate, partial/unverifiable states and stale-summary-on-filter-change are all red before; the 'tampered on the LAST page' case is the one that catches an early-exit sweep.
verdicts.notes: Read-only GET under requireOrgRead, same tenant gate as /api/audit; no wire change to anything consumed outside the repo. Every new features/admin/audit file is planned under 200. Touches data-model.md alongside security A (doc only).

verdicts.title: Status-transition consequences in one module: every close fires them, not PATCH
verdicts.revise: planRecTransition({from:'dismissed', to:'done'}) must emit BOTH 'close-memory' and 'reopen-decision' (today route.ts:146-160 clears the standing dismissal on ANY non-dismissed post-state, done included); add it as an acceptance case so the refactor cannot leave a done gap permanently suppressed.
verdicts.ambition_why: Moves the meaning of a status change out of one HTTP handler so the rescan witness (the only trustworthy close) finally reaches Org Memory; a real architectural seam, not a tidy-up.
verdicts.grounding_why: The three writers have exactly the callers claimed (route.ts:138/148/154 plus db/index re-exports), scans-persist.ts:614-636 creates done rows with only an event, lane-outcomes.ts:360 is the unguarded update, followup-claims.ts:25-26 says what the card quotes.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Persist-path and lane-path cases are red before; the route cases pin existing behaviour, but the transition table as written is missing the dismissed->done row (the revise), so a wrong build would pass today's 7 cases.
verdicts.notes: scans-persist.ts overlaps security A and github-data B. No run-1 overlap. Keep the post-commit call in the appendScanObservations best-effort block as planned; it must not run inside the transaction.

verdicts.title: Sandbox commit previews its extent, lands as one claim with per-item outcomes
verdicts.ambition_why: Puts the sandbox commit on the one claim path the ledger, MCP and loop already use, with a preview and per-item outcomes; the kind of consolidation a principal would insist on.
verdicts.grounding_why: PATCH loop at :122-130, open-only committableRecs at :41, conflated disabled reason at :113-114, status-only PATCH write in scans-recommendations.ts:84-90, hard-coded note in handoff/route.ts, getRecommendationOrgSlug already exported.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Plan/summary/outcome model cases and the single-POST DOM case are red before; the origin-less handoff case is the right regression guard for the untouched default branch.
verdicts.notes: The handoff route today REQUIRES org (400 without it); the card's resolve-then-gate for the sandbox origin is additive and mirrors the per-id PATCH. Behaviourally coupled to roadmap A (the sandbox stops calling the [id] PATCH that A refactors) but no file overlap. RoadmapSandboxParts.tsx at 298 is correctly left alone.

verdicts.title: One requireOrgAdmin door + a guard: no owner/admin route admits the public org
verdicts.revise: Make the guard accept an explicit in-code PUBLIC_ORG comparison (=== / !== PUBLIC_ORG before the gate) as a satisfying refusal, not only requireOrgAdmin(/refusePublicOrgAdmin(: 16 further owner/admin routes (goals/[id], local/{autopilot,drive,pairing,probe,repo,runner/merge}, loop/*, report/foundation/{pr,pr-batch,secrets}, report/passport/{overrides,pr}) already refuse public that way and carry no helper call, so as written the ALLOWLIST would grow to ~16 reasons and the rule is back to 'enforced where someone remembered'.
verdicts.ambition_why: Closes the gap the ADR itself recorded, with a door and a self-testing guard; the right move after two per-route sweeps.
verdicts.grounding_why: The 8 open routes, orgPost.ts:38, authz.ts:308/350 and the ADR line are exact; the guard design undercounts how many routes satisfy the rule via PUBLIC_ORG rather than the helper.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Guard red today naming the 8 routes, seeded comment-only violation, stale-allowlist self-test, and two cases drive the real authz module.
verdicts.notes: Policy-tighten only; nothing widens. Write set is 18 edited + 4 new files, over the ~15 floor, but 8 are one-line vi.mock factory additions. No run-1 overlap. Must strip comments but keep string literals (min role is a string), as the card already states.

verdicts.title: Invite a whole team in one paste: preflight vs roster and pending, then commit
verdicts.ambition_why: A real UX leap for onboarding with a shared client/server classifier, but it is a bulk form over an existing action, not a new capability.
verdicts.grounding_why: One target per submit at MemberInvites.tsx:58-82, unconditional insert at invites.ts:28-49, Invite indexes only orgId/status, route never reads the roster, MembersTab loads both lists, file is 199 lines.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Parser/classifier/batch-route cases are red before and the 'createInvite called ONCE' plus per-refusal 'never called' assertions catch an over-eager build; the single-target guard pins the old body.
verdicts.notes: Batch cap 25, owner gate, public refusal and role cap reused; no new audit action. MemberInvites.tsx extraction (hook + preview) is planned and required under the 200 cap. No overlap with any other card beyond context-map.json.

verdicts.title: Bind a scan token to its forge: a GitHub credential never reaches GitLab
verdicts.ambition_why: Moves a credential-destination rule from two route copies into scanRepository itself so no entry point can forget it; destination binding is the principal's answer.
verdicts.grounding_why: scan.ts:226-227 forge-blind fallback, gitlab/http.ts:44 Bearer, the two routes' inline rule, scan-queue-worker.ts:232 install-token mint and :350 spread, import/route.ts:237-238 single scanOpts, getForgeCredential with zero callers: all exact on the current tree.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Five cases reproduce the leak through real call paths (worker, import, scan.ts ambient and body token); the GitHub guard pins byte-identical behaviour.
verdicts.notes: RUN-1 OVERLAP: src/lib/scan-queue-worker.ts and src/app/api/org/import/route.ts are in the in-flight org-import A card's write set (scan-consequences). Premise lines :232/:350 and :237/:578 may shift once that lands; the premises themselves are not touched by that card's stated scope, but re-anchor before building. Policy-tighten; the only working flow it narrows is nothing (no GitLab credential flows today).

verdicts.title: A self-managed GitLab row is read from its own host, never gitlab.com
verdicts.ambition_why: Makes forge identity travel with the coordinate from adapter to persist instead of being re-guessed from a url in three places; fixes a wrong-tenant read.
verdicts.grounding_why: Host-less parseForgeUrl/source() at scan.ts:195/226, enrich?.() host-less at scan-ingest.ts:133, forgeFromWebUrl host-less with parseGitlabUrl rejecting unknown hosts, scans-persist.ts:134, org-watch.ts:182/281, RepoMeta.forge unused by gitlab source, local.ts:3 vs private-scan-scrub.ts:20-22 contradiction: all verified.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: First-fetch-URL and enrich-host cases are red before and would catch a half-wired host; the no-Installation and local->github guards pin the unchanged paths.
verdicts.notes: Today a self-managed import already splits rows (watch row 'gitlab:group/proj' forge github via import, scan row 'group/proj' via persist), so the card's 'no migration' claim holds and it reduces the split rather than creating one. Overlaps security A (scans-persist, org-watch), roadmap A (scans-persist), and github-data A (scan.ts, sequenced after A as the card says). Fails closed on a non-public host via isSafePublicHttpsUrl; internal-GitLab on self-hosted is a stated residue.

verdicts.title: Tier revocation scoped to its granting subscription: one decision for all three
verdicts.ambition_why: Closes a recorded registry deviation by making revocation source-scoped through one pure decision; a correctness fix a principal would prioritise over features.
verdicts.grounding_why: retainedHigherPlan rank-only at :81-84, downgradeSubscription and the refund branch (:321-336, no Subscription write) as two copies, upsert at :240-243, Subscription one-row-per-org with stripeId, registry-map deviation, the stale :553 known gap vs currentSubscription at :107-121.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Same-tier and lower-tier replacement plus refund-of-non-grantor are red before; the grantor-is-dying, null-grantor and manual-override guards pin existing behaviour.
verdicts.notes: Billing note applied: changes no product, price, grant mapping or payer; it only stops a revoke from removing a tier a different, live subscription is paying for. Residual: decideTierRevocation should treat Subscription.status as part of 'current' (an inactive record's stripeId must not shield), worth a case. src/lib/billing/ does not exist yet; both checkout cards create it (different files). Docs overlap only with checkout B.

verdicts.title: The checkout return banner follows the purchase until it lands, not a claim
verdicts.ambition_why: Replaces an unconditional 'Payment received' with a state machine that ends; honest async UI at the most anxious moment, built from facts the system already holds.
verdicts.grounding_why: successUrl without checkout id at :104-108, static copy at :50-51, credits-only param read at :18-19, SDK 0.48.1 CHECKOUT_ID placeholder / orders.list checkoutId / externalCustomerId, CreditLedger externalId 'polar:<orderId>', and the retry-throws at :213/:237/:253 all verified.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Model, 404-on-foreign-org, landed-vs-paid ledger lookup, polling-stops and no-checkout_id cases are all red before; both guards pin existing dismiss and error behaviour.
verdicts.notes: Billing note applied: read-only status route, successUrl gains a query param only; nothing paid for, priced, granted or charged changes. New route must be added to billing.public.test.ts (listed as shared). BillingReturnNotice.tsx 74->165 stays under 300; overviewBilling.ts 29->45 under 200. Docs overlap only with checkout A.

verdicts.title: One cron-job table: health readiness, vercel.json and every precondition derive
verdicts.ambition_why: Declares the schedule once and derives parity, readiness and preconditions from it; ends five divergent copies of one rule and makes a dead cron visible.
verdicts.grounding_why: vercel.json's five crons, autoscanReadiness rescan-only, the duplicated timingSafeEqual vs cronSecretMatches, purge/athena 503 vs digest/rescan/probe 200 skip, rescan's partial run at :84-85, DEPLOY.md:75 and the archived P1 finding all exact.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Parity test with a seeded mismatch, readiness matrix, the 200->503 flip (digest/route.test.ts:266-274 flips), health crons key; purge and anonymous-health guards pin preserved behaviour.
verdicts.notes: RUN-1 OVERLAP (shared surface only): src/app/api/cron/athena/route.ts is in the in-flight athena A write set; the card correctly declares athena in the table but leaves its call site untouched. Gate 'direction' is right: a DB-less digest/rescan/probe turns red unless CRON_ALLOW_NO_DB=1. cron-jobs.ts appears in both write_set and new_files (harmless).

verdicts.title: An error screen you can act on: retries that count, a prefilled report, Sentry
verdicts.ambition_why: Solid UX hygiene (escalation, redacted report link, Sentry capture, retiring a forked boundary) rather than a product-shaping move.
verdicts.grounding_why: console.error-only at RouteError.tsx:44-46, global-error.tsx:25 as the sole .tsx captureException, server-only onRequestError, report error.tsx:49 reset()-only, FEEDBACK_URL consumed by footer/privacy/terms only, token pages without their own error.tsx: all verified.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Escalation, path-scoped key, token/query redaction, no-message-leak, storage-throws and refresh-before-reset are red before; capture-once is the case that catches a naive useEffect.
verdicts.notes: src/lib/api/respond.ts also calls captureException (server side), consistent with the card's .tsx-only claim. No overlap with any other card. RouteError.tsx 94->150 under 300.
